title: When did the rock move?
hook: A break can put layers out of alignment.

knows: Sedimentary rocks can occur in layers.
doesNotKnow: A movement that offsets a layer follows its formation.

misconception: A fault must be older than every layer it cuts.
objective: Use an offset to infer relative event order.

claims.text: In the pictured model, a fault cuts and offsets both depicted layers; the displacement must postdate formation of the displaced layers. The diagram does not constrain layers that are not cut.
claims.source: Source lead for independent verification: US Geological Survey, National Geologic Map Database, https://www.usgs.gov/programs/national-geologic-map-database; the specific supporting text has not been checked.

claims.text: The stage is a schematic model, with stated example values or sample counts; it is not a reconstruction of an observed field site.
Recall: A fault offsets a layer of sandstone. Which happened later? The layer had to exist before the movement displaced it.
claims.source: Relative order or arithmetic under the explicitly stated example conditions.

options: The order is reversed by the labels
